A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LMAPS work. All pages, including equations, figures, tables and appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LMAPS reconstruction results, a synthetic Gaussian-mixture comparison, optimization-step ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains original LMAPS results and adds analytical-solver comparisons, nonlinear-deblurring budget experiments and measurement-conditioning ablations.

M1.justification: The local MAP objective and denoise–optimize–renoise procedure remain. Algorithm 4 makes a limited pseudocode correction, changing the transition covariance from σn−1 I to σ²n−1 I and explicitly returning optimized x′0. The analytical solution tested in v3 was already derived in v1; the PDFs do not establish a broader implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten FFHQ/ImageNet restoration tasks and the same inverse-scattering, CS-MRI and black-hole scenarios. The synthetic mixture example and qualitative cases are retained. Added experiments vary solvers, budgets or conditioning within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds evaluated DMPlug, MMPS, MGDM, MAP-GA and DMAP comparisons across relevant restoration tasks, retaining the previous comparators. DMPlug and DMAP-related work were already mentioned in v1, but their new table entries substantially expand actual comparisons, especially with the closest MAP-based predecessor.

E3.justification: v3 adds FID, switches Table 3's quality column from PSNR to LPIPS, and introduces protocols for solver comparisons, reduced computation and a k2 sweep at 20 NFEs. Existing datasets, image counts, noise settings, checkpoints and Table 4 hyperparameters remain. Table 9's 200-gradient-step reference conflicts with Table 4's 100, leaving that setting unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Gaussian-deblurring step ablation, v3 adds analytical versus gradient-descent optimization for super-resolution and box inpainting (Table 8), nonlinear-deblurring budget sensitivity (Table 9), and measurement-conditioning strength including k2=0 (Table 10). These substantially extend analysis of solver accuracy, computational tradeoffs and dependence on measurements.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains nonlinear-task ± values but removes v1's explicit explanation that they are standard deviations. Best-of-four phase-retrieval selection and mean/standard-deviation reporting over 94 MRI cases remain. No new seed reporting, repeated-run counts or significance procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial baseline and FID results, while Tables 8–10 add solver and sensitivity outcomes. Among retained Table 1 entries, LMAPS FFHQ box-inpainting PSNR changes from 25.17 to 25.02. Table 10 newly reports PSNR increasing from 10.514 at k2=0 to 27.695 at k2=1. Scientific-result Tables 2 and 5–7 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 and new Appendix B replace heuristic covariance assertions with Gaussian covariance bounds and asymptotic expansions, plus a smooth-prior Laplace-isotropy proposition and proofs. Appendix C derives a tempered-posterior interpretation of k. Appendix A adds mathematical analysis of component-selection regions and probabilities.

C1.justification: The core local-MAP framework, unification and reconstruction-performance claims remain. v3 qualifies motivation by acknowledging posterior uncertainty, explicitly relates novelty to DMAP, and omits the surrogate-gradient contribution from the abstract and contribution list, although the conclusion retains it. Claimed wins become 43/60 under expanded comparisons, replacing v1's inconsistent 46/60 and 49/60 statements.

C2.justification: v3 substantially develops the interpretation of covariance assumptions and k as prior tempering. It introduces a reconstruction-fidelity versus distribution-similarity interpretation of FID and explanations of the new solver, budget and conditioning analyses. However, its discussion of a favorable HDR comparison with DMAP lacks a corresponding DMAP result in Table 1.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link and baseline settings, including DMPlug's 1000 epochs and MMPS's 100 steps with N=5. Main hyperparameters and hardware information remain. It removes v1 Section 4.3's surrogate-gradient recipe despite retaining non-differentiable-task results, reducing standalone reproducibility without establishing that the implementation changed.

R1.justification: Xu et al. (2025), already cited in v1, becomes the explicitly closest prior work, DMAP, with clean-space versus latent-space distinctions developed throughout v3. Classical Bayesian inverse-problem references and MGDM, MMPS and FID citations are added. Figure 1 also removes ΠGDM from the depicted unification relationship.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much existing prose remain, with focused revisions to the abstract, motivation, contributions, covariance explanation and related work. Section 4.3 is removed, appendices expand and are renumbered, and an Impact Statement is added. v3 also duplicates baseline and metric paragraphs under Section 5.2 before the actual results in Section 5.3.

P2.justification: v3 changes the main text and references to a two-column layout, extensively resizes and relocates displays, expands Table 1 with baseline rows and FID columns, and adds Tables 8–10. Figure 1 is revised and Figure 2 updates DAPS pseudocode. Existing experimental plots and qualitative reconstruction images are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important weaknesses in v1's covariance justification and comparison with its closest MAP predecessor through assumption-specific proofs, explicit DMAP positioning and direct evaluation. FID and new ablations substantially strengthen assessment of performance and mechanism. Removing surrogate-gradient instructions, conflicting Table 9 step counts and unsupported DMAP/HDR discussion weaken reproducibility and precision, but the theoretical and comparative gains provide a substantial net improvement.
